title: Forward Interest Rates, FRAs, and Term Structure Theories
targetAudiencePersona: Fixed Income Analyst & Quantitative Derivatives Trader
prerequisites: Understanding of continuous compounding and discounting A = P * e^(rT)
Zero rates and zero-coupon curve construction from Chapter 4 Part 1
Concept of over-the-counter contracts and payoff settlements
learningOutcomes: Calculate continuous and discrete forward interest rates implied by any zero rate curve.
Replicate forward borrowing and lending synthetically through spot zero-coupon bonds.
Price and execute settlement calculations for Forward Rate Agreements (FRAs) at time T_1.
Mark to market existing FRA portfolios using current forward rates and risk-free discounting.
Contrast Expectations Theory with Liquidity Preference Theory to interpret upward-sloping yield curves.
Analyze the Orange County municipal bankruptcy to explain how leverage and inverted repo carry destroy balance sheets.

sections.title: Forward Interest Rates: The Implied Cost of Future Money
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Derive the forward rate formula R_F = (R_2*T_2 - R_1*T_1)/(T_2 - T_1) and demonstrate no-arbitrage replication.
keyPoints: Forward rates are the interest rates implied by current zero rates for future borrowing periods.
Synthetically created by borrowing for T_1 and investing for T_2.

sections.title: Forward Rate Agreements (FRAs) Mechanics and Valuation
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Formulate FRA payoffs, advance cash settlement at time T_1, and mid-life valuation.
keyPoints: Fixed payer receives floating rate R_M and pays fixed contract rate R_K.
Settlement occurs at time T_1 discounted by [1 + R_M*(T_2 - T_1)].
Pre-maturity FRA value is discounted difference between current forward rate R_F and fixed rate R_K.
sections.formulaUsed: Settlement = L*(R_M - R_K)*(T_2 - T_1) / [1 + R_M*(T_2 - T_1)]

sections.title: Theories of the Term Structure: Why Yield Curves Slope Upward
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Dissect Expectations Theory vs Liquidity Preference Theory to prove why forward rates exceed expected spot rates.
keyPoints: Expectations Theory claims forward rates equal expected future spot rates (R_F = E[R]).
Liquidity Preference Theory proves investors demand a premium to lock money up for long horizons.
Forward rates systematically exceed expected future spot rates (R_F > E[R]) by a liquidity premium.

sections.title: Orange County Bankruptcy: The $1.6B Repo Leverage Disaster
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Examine Snapshot 4.1 to understand reverse floaters, repo borrowing leverage, and yield curve inversion risk.
keyPoints: Orange County geared $7.5B equity into $20.5B portfolio via $13B short-term repo borrowing.
Invested heavily in inverse floaters betting interest rates would fall.
Six consecutive Fed rate hikes inverted carry, generating $1.6B losses and municipal bankruptcy.

sections.title: The 2007-2009 Interbank Liquidity Freeze
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Analyze Snapshot 4.2 to see how credit mistrust paralyzed the interbank term market.
keyPoints: Subprime mortgage defaults caused interbank trust to collapse.
Commercial paper markets froze as investors refused rollover.
LIBOR-OIS spread spiked to 364 bps, requiring emergency central bank term auction facilities.

misconceptions.misconception: An upward-sloping yield curve proves the market is betting interest rates will rise sharply in the future.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Liquidity Preference Theory proves forward rates are inflated by positive liquidity premiums (R_F > E[R]). Upward slopes exist even when expected future rates are flat.

misconceptions.misconception: An FRA cash settlement at time T_1 pays the full undiscounted interest difference L*(R_M - R_K)*(T_2 - T_1).
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Because interest payments are normally due at the end of the loan period T_2, advance payment at T_1 must be discounted back by dividing by [1 + R_M*(T_2 - T_1)].

misconceptions.misconception: Short-term repo financing can safely fund long-term bond investments indefinitely.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Orange County proved that financing long-term assets with short-term repo creates extreme negative carry when the yield curve inverts, leading to catastrophic margin calls.

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: Suppose the continuous 1-year zero rate is 4.0% per annum and the 2-year continuous zero rate is 4.5% per annum. An analyst wants to determine the continuous forward interest rate for the second year.
activeRecallQuiz.question: What is the continuous forward rate for the second year (from year 1 to year 2)?
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Using the forward rate formula R_F = (R_2*T_2 - R_1*T_1)/(T_2 - T_1): R_F = (0.045*2 - 0.040*1)/(2 - 1) = (0.090 - 0.040)/1 = 0.050 or 5.0% per annum continuous.

coreTakeaways: Forward interest rates are mathematically locked by zero rates via R_F = (R_2*T_2 - R_1*T_1)/(T_2 - T_1).
FRAs allow borrowers and lenders to lock future borrowing costs; settlement at T_1 is discounted by [1 + R_M*tau].
Existing FRAs are valued by discounting the spread between current forward rates and contract fixed rates.
Liquidity Preference Theory explains normal upward yield curves via maturity liquidity premiums (R_F > E[R]).
Orange County suffered a $1.6B bankruptcy by funding long inverse floaters with $13B short repo leverage during Fed hikes.
